title: Decimal operations
blurb: Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals with the decimal point always in the right place.
question: At the campus store you buy 3 bottles of hand sanitizer at $2.79 each and 2 boxes of gloves at $8.45 each, and pay with $30. How much change should you get?

teach.h: It is all about place value
teach.body: Formally, each digit's value depends on its place: tenths (0.1), hundredths (0.01), thousandths (0.001) to the right of the decimal point. Decimal operations follow whole-number methods plus one rule about where the point goes. In plain English: line points up to add or subtract, count decimal places to multiply, and make the divisor a whole number to divide. Estimate first so a misplaced point jumps out.

head: Place
Value
Digit in 3.462
teach.caption: Trailing zeros after the last digit don't change the value: 0.6 = 0.60 = 0.600.

items: 12.5 + 3.75 + 0.6: line up the points and fill with zeros: 12.50 + 3.75 + 0.60 = 16.85.
20 − 7.38: write 20 as 20.00, then subtract with borrowing: 20.00 − 7.38 = 12.62.
Count decimal places in the factors: 1 (in 2.4) + 1 (in 1.5) = 2.
Place the point 2 places from the right: 3.60 = 3.6. Estimate: 2 × 2 = 4, close to 3.6. ✓

teach.caption: Moving both points the same number of places keeps the answer the same.

items: The divisor 1.2 has 1 decimal place. Move both points 1 place right: 75.6 ÷ 12.
Divide: 12 goes into 75 six times (72), remainder 3; bring down 6 to get 36; 12 goes into 36 three times.
Put the point straight above its place in 75.6: the answer is 6.3.

teach.h: Powers of 10 just move the point

teach.text: Two decimal slips the TEAS builds wrong answers from: 0.3 × 0.2 = 0.06, not 0.6 (count BOTH factors' places: 1 + 1 = 2), and 3.2 + 0.45 = 3.65, not 0.77 (line up the points, not the last digits).

teach.body: Andre Williams, a nursing student, buys 3 hand sanitizers at $2.79 and 2 boxes of gloves at $8.45. Sanitizer: 3 × 2.79 = $8.37. Gloves: 2 × 8.45 = $16.90. Total: 8.37 + 16.90 = $25.27. Change from $30: 30.00 − 25.27 = $4.73. Check: 25.27 + 4.73 = 30.00. ✓ Estimate: 3 × 3 + 2 × 8 = 25, so about $5 change.

items: Add/subtract: line up the decimal points and fill empty places with zeros.
Multiply: multiply as whole numbers, then give the answer as many decimal places as both factors combined.
Divide: move the divisor's point to make it whole, and move the dividend's point the same number of places.
Estimate first, then check by the inverse operation.

summary: You can now add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals and place the decimal point correctly every time. You also check answers by estimating and by the inverse operation, which exposes the misplaced-point options the TEAS offers.

A.q: A nurse had a 2 L bag of saline. She used 0.65 L, then another 0.4 L. How much saline is left?

whyNot.1: 1.31 subtracts 0.04 instead of 0.4: the 4 was lined up in the hundredths place.
whyNot.2: 1.35 is what is left after the first use only, an intermediate step.
whyNot.3: 1.05 comes from a borrowing slip in 2 − 0.65 (1.45 instead of 1.35), then subtracting 0.4.

A.q: Ground turkey costs $4.85 per pound. What is the cost of 2.6 pounds?
A.why: 485 × 26 = 12,610. The factors have 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places, so 12.610 = $12.61. Estimate: 5 × 2.6 = 13. ✓

whyNot.0: $126.10 places the point after only 2 decimal places instead of 3.
whyNot.1: $9.70 is the cost of 2 pounds only; the 0.6 pound is missing.
whyNot.3: $1.26 places the point 4 places from the right, one place too many.

A.q: A pharmacist divides 6.3 g of powder into doses of 0.45 g each. How many doses does this make?

whyNot.0: 1.4 moves the divisor's point only 1 place (6.3 ÷ 4.5).
whyNot.2: 140 moves the dividend's point one place more than the divisor's.
whyNot.3: 0.14 moves the divisor's point but not the dividend's (6.3 ÷ 45).

B.why: The divisor has 3 decimal places. Move both points 3 places: 840 ÷ 7 = 120. Check: 120 × 0.007 = 0.84.

whyNot.0: 12 moves the dividend's point only 2 places (84 ÷ 7) while the divisor's moved 3.
whyNot.1: 1,200 moves the dividend's point 4 places, one more than the divisor's.
whyNot.2: 0.12 divides 0.84 by 7 without moving the dividend's point.

B.q: Lena buys 3 notebooks at $2.49 each and a pen set for $5.75. She pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?

whyNot.1: $11.76 subtracts the price of one notebook, not three: 20 − 2.49 − 5.75.
whyNot.2: $13.22 is the total cost, an intermediate step; the question asks for the change.
whyNot.3: $7.78 is a borrowing slip in 20.00 − 13.22; check: 13.22 + 7.78 = 21.

C.q: A nursing assistant earns $17.40 per hour and $26.10 per hour for overtime. Last week she worked 40 regular hours and 6.5 overtime hours. How much did she earn?

whyNot.1: $809.10 pays all 46.5 hours at the regular rate of $17.40.
whyNot.3: $712.97 misplaces the point in the overtime pay (16.965 instead of 169.65).

C.q: Brand A saline wipes cost $3.48 for 12 ounces. Brand B costs $5.40 for 20 ounces. Which is the better buy, and by how much per ounce?
C.why: Unit prices: A = 3.48 ÷ 12 = $0.29 per ounce; B = 5.40 ÷ 20 = $0.27 per ounce. B is cheaper by 0.29 − 0.27 = $0.02 per ounce.

whyNot.0: A costs $0.29 per ounce, more than B's $0.27, so A is not the better buy.
whyNot.2: B is cheaper, but the difference is 0.02, not 0.20; the point has slipped one place.
whyNot.3: This inverts the rate: 12 ÷ 3.48 ≈ 3.45 and 20 ÷ 5.40 ≈ 3.70 are ounces per dollar, where the HIGHER number is the better buy, and their difference is not a price.

C.q: A patient weighed 182.4 lb at admission and 176.85 lb at discharge. How much weight did the patient lose?
C.why: Write 182.4 as 182.40 and subtract with borrowing: 182.40 − 176.85 = 5.55 lb. Check: 176.85 + 5.55 = 182.40.

whyNot.0: 6.55 forgets to reduce the ones digit after borrowing from it (12 − 6 instead of 11 − 6).
whyNot.1: 5.65 forgets to reduce the tenths digit after borrowing for the hundredths (14 − 8 instead of 13 − 8).
whyNot.2: 5.19 reads 182.4 as 182.04, putting the 4 in the hundredths place.

reteach.title: Decimals are dollars and cents
reteach.question: You add up a receipt every time you shop. How does stacking dollars over dollars and cents over cents explain the decimal rules?

blocks.body: On a receipt, $12.50, $3.75 and $0.60 stack with dollars over dollars and cents over cents. Nobody adds 50 cents to 3 dollars by mistake, because the decimal points line up. That is the whole addition rule. For multiplying, think "part of a part": 0.3 of 0.2 dollars is 3 tenths of 20 cents, which is 6 cents, $0.06. A part of a part is smaller than both parts.

head: Item
Price
blocks.caption: Points stacked in one column; $0.60 is the same as $0.6.

items: How many 15-cent stamps can $4.50 buy? Think in cents: 450 ÷ 15 = 30.
That is exactly 4.5 ÷ 0.15 with both points moved 2 places.
Changing both amounts to cents changes the numbers, not the answer.

blocks.text: $3.20 plus 45 cents is $3.65, not 77 cents. Line up the points, never the last digits.

explain.body: Line up the decimal points and fill empty places with zeros so every number has the same number of decimal places. Then add or subtract as with whole numbers, borrowing as needed.

test.q: A 7 mL syringe is filled, and 2.36 mL is injected. How much is left in the syringe?

whyNot.0: 5.36 subtracts only the whole number (7 − 2) and keeps the .36.
whyNot.1: 4.74 forgets to reduce the tenths after borrowing for the hundredths.
whyNot.3: 9.36 adds the amounts instead of subtracting.

explain.body: Multiply as if there were no points, then count the decimal places in BOTH factors and give the answer that many places. 1.25 × 0.8: 125 × 8 = 1,000, and 2 + 1 = 3 places, so 1.000 = 1.

test.why: 125 × 8 = 1,000. Three decimal places in total gives 1.000 = 1. Estimate: 1.25 is a bit more than 1, and 0.8 of it is about 1. ✓

whyNot.1: 0.1 places the point 4 places from the right, one too many.
whyNot.2: 10 places the point after only 2 decimal places.
whyNot.3: 0.01 places the point 5 places from the right.

explain.body: Move the divisor's point right until it is a whole number, then move the dividend's point the same number of places. 9.6 ÷ 0.32 becomes 960 ÷ 32.

whyNot.0: 3 moves the dividend only 1 place (96 ÷ 32) while the divisor moved 2.
whyNot.2: 300 moves the dividend 3 places, one more than the divisor.
whyNot.3: 0.3 moves the divisor's point but not the dividend's (9.6 ÷ 32 = 0.3).

explain.body: Multiplying by 10, 100 or 1,000 moves the point 1, 2 or 3 places right; dividing moves it left. Count the zeros, move that many places.

test.q: Each of 1,000 tablets contains 0.025 g of a drug. How many grams of the drug are in all the tablets together?
test.why: × 1,000 moves the point 3 places right: 0.025 → 25 g.

whyNot.0: 2.5 g moves the point only 2 places (× 100).
whyNot.2: 0.25 g moves the point only 1 place (× 10).
